Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors: 3 days of profuse watery diarrhoea (stools nearly every hour while awake), intermittent crampy lower/central abdominal pain (patient rates pain ~6/10 when present), nausea with at least one vomiting episode (noted after drinking milk), subjective fever/hot sensations (no measured temperature), reduced urinary frequency (possible dehydration). Brother has had a similar self-limited diarrhoeal illness. No prior chronic GI history reported.
- Relevant family medical history: Father with stage 3 colon cancer; brother recently had similar diarrhoeal illness (~5 days).
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications): Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition: Patient reports being "an OK weight"; no objective height/weight/BMI recorded. Eats irregularly (often buys own food); currently tolerating fluids but reports solids pass loose.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Social smoker (occasional, social cigarettes). Alcohol: occasional use with heavier drinking once or twice per month.
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): No mood disorder, depression or self-harm risk reported; patient prefers to manage health issues independently.
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Lives with mother and sister; brother does not live with patient. Works in an office (government, Central London). Prefers to continue working where possible and avoids taking time off.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings and impressions:
  - Acute onset (≈3 days) profuse watery diarrhoea with crampy central/lower abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, subjective fever, and decreased urine output consistent with possible dehydration.
  - Household contact (brother) with similar self-limited illness supports an infectious cause.
- Working diagnosis: Acute gastroenteritis, most consistent with acute viral gastroenteritis (high likelihood).
- DDx-aligned differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):
  - Acute viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus) — High likelihood: supported by rapid onset, high stool frequency, nausea/vomiting, subjective fever and household contact.
  - Bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis — Moderate likelihood: possible shared exposure; less likely given household pattern and absence of bloody stools or severe systemic signs.
  - Secondary (transient) lactose intolerance post-infectious — Moderate likelihood: vomiting after milk and possible worsening with dairy intake; may be coexisting consequence of enteric infection.
- Important complications to monitor: Dehydration/electrolyte disturbance (patient reports reduced urine frequency and feeling hot).
- Conflict noted: None identified between transcript and DDx.

Management Plan

- Immediate recommendations provided in consult:
  - Rehydration: Increase fluid intake; encourage oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte/ORS) available over-the-counter.
  - Diet: Start with clear fluids and soft diet (soup, mashed foods), advance as tolerated.
  - Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol for fever/pain (continue as needed; dose not documented).
  - Avoid alcohol while unwell.
- Safety net / follow-up:
  - If symptoms not settling within 48 hours, or if signs of dehydration worsen (markedly reduced urine output, dizziness, fainting, ongoing vomiting, inability to keep fluids down), patient instructed to recontact for reassessment and possible further investigations.
  - Consider further investigations (e.g., clinical assessment, vitals, fluid replacement, stool studies) if not improving or if dehydrated/severe.
- Patient education: Explained likely self-limited gastroenteritis course; advised ORS, fluid replacement, soft diet, avoid alcohol, continue paracetamol for fever/pain.
- No prescriptions or referrals were initiated during this consult.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus) — Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Acute 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea, crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, subjective fever and a household contact with similar illness; rapid, self-limited course typical for viral etiology.
- Bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis (e.g., enterotoxigenic E. coli, Salmonella, Campylobacter) — Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Profuse diarrhoea, cramping and subjective fever could be bacterial; possible shared exposure with brother. Less supported by lack of bloody stools and absence of severe systemic features in this consult.
- Secondary (post-infectious) lactose intolerance — Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Vomiting after milk and known association of transient lactase deficiency following enteric infection; may contribute to dairy-associated symptoms while recovering.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate).
  - Weight/height/BMI and waist circumference.
  - Formal assessment of hydration status (mucous membranes, capillary refill, orthostatic vitals).
  - Urinalysis and point-of-care glucose if dehydration suspected.
  - Stool studies (microscopy/culture/PCR) if symptoms persist or severe.
  - Detailed immunisation status review.
  - Detailed quantification of alcohol use and smoking history (pack-years), drug use screening.
  - Sexual health history/screening (if indicated).
  - Mental health screening (formal) given social/work stressors if concerns arise.
- Internal contradictions between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted; DDx aligns with transcript findings.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Telehealth audio-only consult with some connection/display issues at start. Conversation occasionally had brief overlap and incomplete phrases, but overall clinical history is coherent and sufficient for initial assessment.
